items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: So he had two of the world’s greatest... he started out with Herschel and Lester.

ctx.x: Let me ask you this. You mentioned this other player, you mentioned his tone, and you said you liked his tone. Would you consider that you also have a signature tone, where people can just hear your tone and know that’s you? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

I try, I’ve tried for that to happen, and that’s what I hope is coming across because we in those days we tried to be individual, to be say, oh, yeah, that’s Buddy Tate, that’s Herschel Evans. So that’s what we tried to do then. And you know we didn’t want to like if you got the same teacher, if everybody sounded the same, you didn’t know who’s who. So we didn’t want it that way, you know? So I’ve tried to do it the way so they could say I could be identified.
Now talk to us about when you first started with Basie.

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: playing with Jacq', I got more vibes for one to play when he was in the band than I did with Prez.

ctx.x: Yeah, he really did. Actually, he did a lot of things -- he made me always -- made me want to play. But Jacquet- I got more Jacquet - playing with Jacq', I got more vibes for one to play when he was in the band than I did with Prez. Because when Jacq' came in the band, man, he was really -- he was cooking.

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: But I'd met him now before then

ctx.x: Yeah, you know. And there was money everywhere. So -- oh, yeah. Now by now, I had switched because,

yeah, we'd brought Milton up and he -- no, no. We carried him to Wichita Falls. He come up and work with us about a month, this Milton Thomas on tenor. He came up and worked with us about a month and we went to Wichita Falls to play and we went out and played a week in Wichita Falls and it was -- everybody had money out there, you know. Then there was a band out there that wanted us to join them. So Herschel [Evans] was in this band and he's playing brass alto. But I'd met him now before then, but he --
